Building on our rerandomizatio simulation we can analyze each outcome in turn to assess how the estimators function for that particular simulation scenario.  See the main rerandomizartion report for how the range of estimates across the simulation scenarios changes.


## The datasets missing from this analysis

We didn't run the simulation on all the empirical datasets due to privacy restrictions and computational feasibility.  The datasets dropped are the following:

```{r}
knitr::kable( tibble( `dropped sets` = miss_sets ) )
```


## How do the simulation estimated SEs compare to the actual simulation SE?


```{r}

simdat_meth <- studies$UniqueID %>%
  set_names() %>%
  map( \(file) {
    fname = paste0( SIM_DIR, file, ".rds" )
    # check if file exists
    if ( file.exists( fname ) ) {
      res <- read_rds( fname )
      summarize_simulation_results( res, "method" )
    } else {
      NULL
    }
  } )  %>% 
  bind_rows( .id = "UniqueID" ) %>%
  as_tibble()

ggplot( simdat_meth, aes( SE, ESEhat ) ) +
  facet_wrap( ~ method ) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_fixed() +
  geom_abline( slope=1, intercept=0, lty=2 )

```


## How do the SEs we get from simulation compare to empirical SEhats?


```{r}


cc <- filter( combined,
              Covariates=="best" ) %>%
  dplyr::select(UniqueID, Estimator, Estimand, ATE_hat_std, SE_hat_std ) %>%
  rename( method = Estimator ) %>%
  mutate( has_FI = str_detect( method, "FI" ) )

simdat_meth <- simdat_meth %>%
  left_join(cc, by=c("UniqueID", "method"))


ggplot( simdat_meth, aes( SE_hat_std, SE, color=UniqueID ) ) +
#  facet_grid( has_FI ~ Estimand ) +
  facet_wrap( ~ method, nrow=2 ) +
  #facet_wrap( ~UniqueID ) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_fixed() +
  geom_abline( slope=1, intercept=0, lty=2 )
```


## How do ranges reduce by going within estimand

For each outcome, we can see how the range of the estimates goes down when looking within each estimand.
We do this first for the ATE, and then for the SE estimates.

```{r}
simW <- simdat %>%
  dplyr::select( UniqueID, Estimand, runID, ratioSE, rangeATE ) %>%
  pivot_wider( names_from = "Estimand", values_from = c( "rangeATE", "ratioSE" ) ) %>%
  mutate( rat_ATE_C = rangeATE_Cluster / rangeATE_Overall,
          rat_ATE_P = rangeATE_Person / rangeATE_Overall,
          rat_SE_C = ratioSE_Cluster / ratioSE_Overall,
          rat_SE_P = ratioSE_Person / ratioSE_Overall ) %>%
  group_by( UniqueID ) %>%
  summarise( across( c( rat_ATE_C, rat_ATE_P, rat_SE_C, rat_SE_P ), list( mn=mean, sd=sd ) ) )

ss_W <- summary_stats %>%
  filter( Covariates=="best" ) %>%
  
  dplyr::select( UniqueID, Estimand, ratioSE, rangeATE ) %>%
  pivot_wider( names_from = "Estimand", values_from = c( "rangeATE", "ratioSE" ) ) %>%
  mutate( rat_ATE_C = rangeATE_Cluster / rangeATE_Overall,
          rat_ATE_P = rangeATE_Person / rangeATE_Overall,
          rat_SE_C = ratioSE_Cluster / ratioSE_Overall,
          rat_SE_P = ratioSE_Person / ratioSE_Overall ) 

fin_res <- left_join( ss_W, simW, 
                      by = "UniqueID", suffix = c( "_true", "" ) )

fin_res
names( fin_res ) <- str_replace( names( fin_res ), "Cluster", "C" )
names( fin_res ) <- str_replace( names( fin_res ), "Person", "P" )
names( fin_res ) <- str_replace( names( fin_res ), "Overall", "All" )
fin_res %>%
  dplyr::select( UniqueID, contains("ATE") ) %>%
  rename_with(~ str_remove(., "ATE_")) %>%
  knitr::kable( digits = 2 )
```

The above table shows, for each dataset, the average fraction of the range of the ATE estimates for the cluster and person estimands relative to the overall range.
The first columns show the reduction in the real empirical results, and the second set of columns show the average reduction in the simulations.
The `sd` columns show how much these numbers vary across the individual simulation runs.


We do the same for the SEs:

```{r}
fin_res %>%
  dplyr::select( UniqueID, contains("SE") ) %>%
  rename_with(~ str_remove(., "SE_")) %>%
  knitr::kable( digits = 2 )
```


And now some viz:

```{r}
names( fin_res )
finW <- fin_res %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -c( UniqueID, rangeATE_All, ratioSE_All ),
    names_to="col", values_to="value" ) %>%
  separate_wider_regex( col, 
                        c( measure = ".*", "_", Estimand = "C|P", "_?", sim = ".*" ) ) %>%
  mutate( measure = paste0( measure, sim ) ) %>%
  dplyr::select( -sim ) %>%
  pivot_wider( names_from = measure, values_from = value ) 


ggplot( finW, aes( rat_ATE, rat_ATEmn ) ) +
  facet_wrap( ~ Estimand ) +
  geom_errorbar( aes( ymin=rat_ATEmn-rat_ATEsd, ymax=rat_ATEmn+rat_ATEsd ), width=0, col="grey" ) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_fixed( xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1) ) +
  geom_abline( slope=1, intercept=0, lty=2 )+
  labs( y = "Simulation (average proportion ATE range)",
        x = "Empirical (actual reduction ATE range)",
        title = "Ratio of ranges of ATE estimates" )

```

We are seeing no strong relationship between how much the range of ATE estimates goes down across the simulations and how much it went down in our empirical data. For the Person estimand, the ratios in the simulation tend to be very small, suggesting that the person-weighted estimators are much closer together in the simulation than they are in the actual data.



For the standard errors, we are not seeing much reduction in the ratio of largest to smallest standard error when we move to the two estimands.  That said, the simulation does suggest that the reduction of the SE ratio for some studies is anomolous.

```{r}

ggplot( finW, aes( rat_SE, rat_SEmn ) ) +
  facet_wrap( ~ Estimand ) +
    geom_errorbar( aes( ymin=rat_SEmn-rat_SEsd, ymax=rat_SEmn+rat_SEsd ), width=0, col="grey" ) +
  geom_point() +
  coord_fixed( xlim=c(0,1), ylim=c(0,1) ) +
  geom_abline( slope=1, intercept=0, lty=2 )+
  labs( y = "Simulation (average reduction SE ratio)",
        x = "Empirical (actual reduction SE ratio)",
        title = "Ratio of ratios of SE estimates" )
```
